risk_surfaces: _default_planning_model behavioral shift (swe_af/execution/schemas.py:756-809): when SWE_DEFAULT_RUNTIME=open_code or codex is set without any model env var, the planning reasoners (pm, architect, tech_lead, sprint_planner) now receive the runtime's base default (openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 or gpt-5.3-codex/gpt-5.5) instead of sonnet. The docstring documents this as intentional (lines 773-788), but any deployment that set SWE_DEFAULT_RUNTIME to opt into a runtime while relying on the implicit sonnet planning model will see a silent model swap. Callers of _default_planning_model() with no runtime argument (the existing call signature) are unaffected; only explicit SWE_DEFAULT_RUNTIME deployments without SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL/AI_MODEL change behavior.

HARNESS_MODEL scoping change affects existing Docker deployments (swe_af/execution/schemas.py:731-733, go/internal/config/resolve.go:247-249): previously, HARNESS_MODEL was the first env var consulted for every runtime. Deployments that set HARNESS_MODEL to an openrouter/... model without also setting SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL or AI_MODEL, and that run claude_code or codex, will now get their runtime's native default instead of the openrouter id. This is a correctness fix (the old behavior produced ~1s empty completions per the docstring at line 608), but it changes runtime behavior for affected deployments.

Go port incomplete tier-model resolution in FastResolveModels (go/internal/config/fastconfig.go:133-177): the Python fast_resolve_models applies tier env vars (SWE_MODEL_LOW/MED/HIGH) between the env cascade and config model layers (swe_af/fast/schemas.py:185-190), but the Go port's FastResolveModels skips tierModelsFromEnv entirely. Any deployment using SWE_MODEL_MED or SWE_MODEL_HIGH to steer fast-build roles will see those env vars silently ignored by the Go node. The main-path ResolveRuntimeModels in resolve.go:394-401 does include tier resolution, so only the fast path is affected.

Go port adds SWE_CODEX_AUTH_MODE to providerEnvKeys (go/internal/config/config_test.go:20): this key is now cleared in every test that calls clearProviderEnv. If any test in the same process runs codex-related code after a clearProviderEnv call without re-setting it, the codex auth mode will be empty/auto, potentially affecting test ordering sensitivity. The current test file is safe because each subtest re-sets its own env, but future tests added to this package that share the process could inherit an empty SWE_CODEX_AUTH_MODE from a preceding test.

Go Dockerfile installs Python3+pytest (go/Dockerfile:76): this adds ~50MB to the Go node image. The comment says it's needed for the verifier role and evidence-based audits on Python repos. If the Go node's verifier spawns pytest in a way that conflicts with the Python node's pytest (same named volume, different Python paths), verification results could diverge between the two implementations. The two nodes should not share a workspaces volume in production (they have distinct NODE_IDs), but docker-compose.go.yml should be checked to confirm this.

Codex wrapper script in both Dockerfiles (Dockerfile:24-49, go/Dockerfile:91-116): the wrapper is functionally identical in both files. Any divergence in future edits (e.g., one Dockerfile gets a new auth mode check and the other does not) would silently cause different codex auth behavior between the Python and Go deployments.

Go config_test.go adds ci_fixer_model to AllModelFields iteration tests (lines 108-117, 123-128): the Python BuildConfig defaults test (tests/test_model_config.py) does not check ci_fixer_model specifically. If ci_fixer's default diverges between Python and Go (e.g., Go sets it to haiku instead of sonnet for claude_code), no Python test catches it. The Go tests at config_test.go:705-720 cover this, but cross-language consistency depends on manual alignment.
pr_narrative: This PR does three distinct things. First, it ports the Python configuration and model-resolution logic from swe_af/execution/schemas.py and swe_af/fast/schemas.py into a new Go package at go/internal/config/ (resolve.go, fastconfig.go, config_test.go), giving the Go node identical runtime/model cascading behavior to the Python node. Second, it fixes a cross-runtime leak: HARNESS_MODEL (a Docker-baked OpenCode ecosystem variable used for OpenCode's small_model interpolation) was incorrectly being consulted for claude_code and codex runtimes, silently injecting openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 into CLIs that cannot consume it. The fix scopes HARNESS_MODEL to open_code only in both _default_model_from_env (Python, swe_af/execution/schemas.py:709-737) and defaultModelFromEnv (Go, go/internal/config/resolve.go:245-255). Third, _default_planning_model (swe_af/execution/schemas.py:756-809) gains an optional runtime parameter and changes behavior: when SWE_DEFAULT_RUNTIME is explicitly set to open_code or codex (with no model env vars), it now returns that runtime's base default instead of the historical sonnet fallback. The Dockerfiles change in tandem: go/Dockerfile adds the Claude Code CLI (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code, line 86) and Python3+pytest for the verifier role, and both Dockerfiles get a codex wrapper script that enforces SWE_CODEX_AUTH_MODE at container entry. .env.example gets documentation updates for the Claude Code OAuth token path, the AI_MODEL cascade warning, and Codex auth modes.
intent_gaps: The PR description says 'Local Repository Review' with no actual description text, making it impossible to verify intent without reading every changed file. The actual scope (Go config port + HARNESS_MODEL scoping + planning model behavioral fix + Dockerfile tooling) is three orthogonal changes.

_default_planning_model's behavioral change (swe_af/execution/schemas.py:756-809) is documented in the docstring but is not called out in any changelog, migration note, or breaking-change notice. A deployer with SWE_DEFAULT_RUNTIME=open_code and no model env var will silently get a different planning model after this PR merges. The docstring says this is the intended fix, but there is no release note or upgrade guide entry.

The Go port's FastResolveModels is missing tier-model resolution (go/internal/config/fastconfig.go:133-177). The Python fast_resolve_models supports SWE_MODEL_LOW/MED/HIGH (swe_af/fast/schemas.py, no explicit tier step visible in the fast path, but swe_af/execution/schemas.py's resolve_runtime_models does). The Go tests for fast config (config_test.go:809-891) have no tier-model test cases, suggesting this gap was not detected during review.

The Go config_test.go adds TestResolveRuntimeModels_Codex (line 312) and TestFastResolveModels_HarnessModelScopedToOpenCode (line 239), but there is no corresponding test in the Python test suite (tests/test_model_config.py, tests/fast/test_schemas.py) for the codex chatgpt auth mode's interaction with HARNESS_MODEL scoping on the fast path. The Python fast tests (tests/fast/test_schemas.py) test HARNESS_MODEL scoping for open_code and claude_code but not for codex.

The _default_planning_model Python change adds a `runtime` parameter (line 804), but there is no Go equivalent function that accepts a runtime parameter. Go's DefaultPlanningModel() (resolve.go:277-288) always derives runtime from the environment. If the SDK layer calls planning reasoners with an explicit runtime argument, the Go node cannot honor it for the planning model selection.
unrelated_changes: go/Dockerfile installs Python3 and python3-pytest (line 76): this is infrastructure for the Go node's verifier role, not a config/model change. It belongs in a Docker/infrastructure PR or should be explicitly called out in the PR description.

.env.example documentation expansion: the changes to .env.example (lines 28-34 SWE_CODEX_AUTH_MODE, lines 49-53 AI_MODEL cascade warning, lines 59-65 Claude Code OAuth) are documentation updates that should be in their own docs PR or at least called out separately. They are correct and useful, but they bloat a config-behavioral diff.

README.md line 406: a one-line clarification about HARNESS_MODEL only affecting open_code. This is a doc-only change triggered by the HARNESS_MODEL fix and could be bundled with the .env.example doc updates.

diff_patches.README.md:
For Codex with ChatGPT subscription auth, install the Codex CLI on the host, run `codex login`, leave `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset for this process, and set `SWE_CODEX_AUTH_MODE=chatgpt` or `auto`. For OpenAI API-platform billing, set `SWE_CODEX_AUTH_MODE=api_key` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
 
-> **Codex deployments using the Docker image must set `SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-5.3-codex` on the environment** (or pass `models: {"default": "gpt-5.3-codex"}` in every build's `config`). The image bakes `HARNESS_MODEL=openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6` as an OpenCode fallback, and SWE-AF's model-resolution env cascade reads `HARNESS_MODEL` — so without `SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL` set, the Codex CLI receives an OpenRouter model id it can't handle and the Product Manager reasoner fails in ~13s. Setting `SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL` makes the cascade pin every role to the Codex model.
+> The Docker image bakes `HARNESS_MODEL=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` so OpenCode's `small_model` config interpolation always has a value. `HARNESS_MODEL` only affects the `open_code` runtime — `claude_code` and `codex` deployments resolve their own runtime defaults (codex picks its model by auth mode) and can override per role via `SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL` / `models` as usual.
 
 > Codex CLI's `workspace-write` sandbox uses bubblewrap (`bwrap`) and needs Linux user namespaces enabled on the host. Most production Linux hosts and managed container runtimes (Railway, etc.) allow this by default, but local Docker on WSL2 or hardened environments may refuse with `bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace`. If the verifier reports that error, the coder ran but couldn't write files — enable user namespaces on the host before relying on the codex runtime there.

+class TestDockerfileHarnessModelDefault(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Guard: the HARNESS_MODEL the images bake must be the OpenRouter auto
+    default the code and README promise. Docker layer caching plus the env
+    cascade means a drifted value silently becomes what every OpenRouter-only
+    deployment actually runs (that is exactly how kimi-k2.6 shipped)."""
+
+    def _dockerfile_value(self, relpath: str) -> str:
+        root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+        with open(os.path.join(root, relpath), encoding="utf-8") as fp:
+            for line in fp:
+                if line.startswith("ENV HARNESS_MODEL="):
+                    return line.strip().split("=", 1)[1]
+        raise AssertionError(f"no ENV HARNESS_MODEL line in {relpath}")
+
+    def test_python_image_matches_auto_default(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._dockerfile_value("Dockerfile"), _OPENROUTER_AUTO_DEFAULT_MODEL
+        )
+
+    def test_go_image_matches_auto_default(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._dockerfile_value(os.path.join("go", "Dockerfile")),
+            _OPENROUTER_AUTO_DEFAULT_MODEL,
+        )
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
